kind: actual model-selected structured lookup with local host execution
task: Review the consent rules for a reorganisation of the provider in CONTRACT-01 for the customer. Does an internal reorganisation require consent? Ownership and continued responsibility are not yet confirmed.

actual_tool_result.text: Neither party may assign any rights or obligations under this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party. In addition, Provider must obtain Customer’s prior written consent before a change of control of Provider takes effect. That consent is not required for a reorganization within a wholly owned group if Provider remains responsible for its obligations under this Agreement. Any attempted but non-permitted assignment is void. This Agreement will be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their permitted successors and assigns.
actual_tool_result.source_location: Agreement - Executed v2.txt, Key Terms, Other Changes to Standard Terms, Teaching Adaptation 1

Source: KT-1 (Agreement - Executed v2.txt, Key Terms, Other Changes to Standard Terms, Teaching Adaptation 1)

Triggers identified:
1. Assignment of rights or obligations – requires Customer's prior written consent.
2. Change of control of Provider – requires Customer's prior written consent before it takes effect.

Exception: Consent is not required for a reorganisation within a wholly owned group if Provider remains responsible for its obligations under the Agreement.

Application to internal reorganisation:
• The label 'internal reorganisation' does not by itself establish that an assignment or a change of control will occur.
• Even if a trigger applies, the group exception may relieve the consent requirement—but only if (a) the reorganisation is within a wholly owned group, and (b) Provider remains responsible for its obligations.
• Ownership structure and continued responsibility are stated as unconfirmed.

Conclusion: The consent position cannot be determined on available facts. Evidence is needed to establish (1) whether the transaction constitutes an assignment or change of control, and (2) whether the exception conditions are satisfied.
